torvosaurus:enwiki:12.title: Torvosaurus (Fauna and habitat in North America)

torvosaurus:enwiki:15.title: Torvosaurus (Fauna and habitat in South America)

facts.statement: Torvosaurus lived during the Middle to Late Jurassic periods, specifically from the Callovian to the Tithonian ages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Middle - Late Jurassic (Callovian to Tithonian),

facts.statement: The genus Torvosaurus was named by Peter Malcolm Galton and James Alvin Jensen in 1979.
facts.quote: authority: Galton & Jensen, 1979

facts.statement: Torvosaurus contains two recognized species, T. tanneri and T. gurneyi, and one unnamed species from Germany.
facts.quote: It contains two currently recognized species, Torvosaurus tanneri and Torvosaurus gurneyi, plus a third unnamed species from Germany.

facts.statement: Fossils of Torvosaurus have been found in what is now Colorado, Portugal, Germany, and possibly England, Spain, Tanzania, and Uruguay.
facts.quote: during the Callovian to Tithonian ages of the late Middle and Late Jurassic period in what is now Colorado, Portugal, Germany, and possibly England, Spain, Tanzania, and Uruguay.

facts.statement: Torvosaurus tanneri measured around 9 meters long and weighed approximately 2 to 2.4 metric tons.
facts.quote: Measuring around 9 m long and weighing approximately 2 - 2.4 MT, T. tanneri was among the largest terrestrial carnivores in North America during the Late Jurassic.

facts.statement: Specimens of Torvosaurus gurneyi have been measured up to 10 meters in length and 4 to 5 metric tons in body mass.
facts.quote: Specimens of Torvosaurus gurneyi were measured up to 10 m in length and 4 - 5 MT in body mass.

facts.statement: The first remains referable to Torvosaurus were discovered in 1899 by Elmer Riggs in the Freeze-out Hills of southeastern Wyoming.
facts.quote: The first discovered remains referable to Torvosaurus were discovered in 1899 by Elmer Riggs in the "Freeze-out Hills" of southeastern Wyoming, 11 mi northwest of Medicine Bow.

facts.statement: Remains of a large theropod now believed to be Torvosaurus were discovered in the Tendaguru Formation of Tanzania and named Megalosaurus ingens by Werner Janensch in 1920.
facts.quote: More remains of a large theropod that is now believed to have been Torvosaurus were discovered in the Tendaguru Formation of Tanzania and was named "Megalosaurus" ingens by Werner Janensch in 1920

facts.statement: Teeth of a member of the genus Torvosaurus were described from the Tacuarembó Formation of Uruguay by Soto et al. in 2020.
facts.quote: Soto et al. (2020) described teeth of a member of the genus Torvosaurus from the Tacuarembó Formation of Uruguay.

facts.statement: In 1971, Vivian Jones discovered a gigantic theropod thumb claw at the Calico Gulch Quarry in Moffat County, Colorado.
facts.quote: In 1971, Vivian Jones of Delta, Colorado, in the Calico Gulch Quarry in Moffat County, discovered a single gigantic thumb claw of a theropod.

facts.statement: The specific name tanneri honors Nathan Eldon Tanner, a first counselor in the First Presidency of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.
facts.quote: The specific name tanneri comes from the, first counselor in the First Presidency of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, Nathan Eldon Tanner.

facts.statement: In 1985, James Alvin Jensen reported additional material including the first skull elements of Torvosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1985, Jensen could report a considerable amount of additional material, among it being the first skull elements.

facts.statement: The holotype and paratypes of Torvosaurus represented at least three individuals: two adults and one juvenile.
facts.quote: The holotype and paratypes represented at least three individuals, these being two adults and a juvenile.

facts.statement: In 1992, fossils containing skull, shoulder girdle, pelvic, and rib elements were found at Como Bluff in Wyoming.
facts.quote: In 1992, fossils of a large theropod found at Como Bluff in Wyoming contained skull, shoulder girdle, pelvic, and rib elements.

facts.statement: Most researchers now regard Edmarka rex and Brontoraptor as junior synonyms of Torvosaurus tanneri.
facts.quote: Most researchers now regard both Edmarka rex and "Brontoraptor" as junior synonyms of Torvosaurus tanneri.

facts.statement: In 2012, a 55% complete undescribed specimen of Torvosaurus was discovered in the Skull Creek Quarry in Colorado.
facts.quote: In 2012, a still undescribed, 55% complete specimen was discovered in Colorado in the Skull Creek Quarry, which is an exposure of the Morrison Formation.

facts.statement: It is debated whether teeth from Tanzania and Uruguay belong to Torvosaurus, as some researchers consider them undiagnostic and similar to other theropods like carcharodontosaurids.
facts.quote: However, Rauhut et al. (2020) consider the teeth to be undiagnostic, being coherent in size and shape with a variety of other theropods (including carcharodontosaurids), thus considering their attribution to the genus to be problematic.

facts.statement: Researchers debate whether Megalosaurus ingens from Tanzania and Uruguayan teeth represent the same taxon as Torvosaurus, noting shared features but lacking derived characteristics to confirm synonymy.
facts.quote: Soto et al. (2020) described teeth of a member of the genus Torvosaurus from the Tacuarembó Formation of Uruguay. The authors noted that some of the specimens of "Megalosaurus" ingens figured by Werner Janensch share the features of the Uruguayan material and stated that the materials from Tanzania and Uruguay may represent the same taxon, due to geographical proximity, but ultimately concluded that, based on only teeth, they do not share any derived characteristics to distinguish them from the described species of the genus, T. tanneri and T. gurneyi.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Edmarka rex and Brontoraptor are junior synonyms of Torvosaurus tanneri, as their original specimens lack detailed descriptions for confirmation.
facts.quote: In 2014, Sebastian Dalman suggested that while Edmarka rex and "Brontoraptor" are most likely junior synonyms of T. tanneri, the original incomplete specimens assigned to these taxa require re-examination as they lack detailed osteological descriptions to confirm or dispute this supposed synonymy.

facts.statement: In 2000, Octávio Mateus and Miguel Telles Antunes referred Portuguese material to Torvosaurus sp.
facts.quote: In 2000, material from Portugal was referred to a Torvosaurus sp. by Octávio Mateus and Miguel Telles Antunes.

facts.statement: In 2006, fossils from the Portuguese Lourinhã Formation were assigned to Torvosaurus tanneri.
facts.quote: In 2006, fossils from the Portuguese Lourinhã Formation were referred to Torvosaurus tanneri.

facts.statement: In 2012, Matthew Carrano and colleagues concluded that Portuguese fossils could not be identified more precisely than Torvosaurus sp.
facts.quote: In 2012, however, Matthew Carrano and colleagues concluded that this material could not be more precisely determined than a Torvosaurus sp.

facts.statement: Eggs with and without embryos found in Portugal in 2013 and 2014 were referred to Torvosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2013 and 2014, eggs with and without embryos were reported from Portugal and referred to Torvosaurus.

facts.statement: The Portuguese species was named Torvosaurus gurneyi in 2014 to honor James Gurney, the creator of the Dinotopia series.
facts.quote: The species from Portugal was named T. gurneyi in honor of James Gurney in 2014, the creator of the Dinotopia series of books.

facts.statement: Torvosaurus gurneyi is the largest named European theropod, though a larger isolated vertebra from Spain may belong to it or a related taxon.
facts.quote: It is the largest named theropod known from Europe, although an isolated anterior caudal vertebra from the Vega Formation in Spain, which may belong to Torvosaurus or a closely related taxon, is about 15% larger than the one found on T. gurneyi.

facts.statement: One of the describers of T. gurneyi argued that giant vertebrae from the Vega Formation likely belong to that species.
facts.quote: One of the describers of T.gurneyi argued the giant vertebrae from the Vega Formation likely does belong to T.gurneyi.

facts.statement: In 2020, Soto and colleagues described a tooth from Uruguay as belonging to an unnamed new species of Torvosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2020, Soto and colleagues described FC-DPV 2971, a tooth from Uruguay, as belonging to a new unnamed species of Torvosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2020, a fragmentary maxilla from the middle Callovian Ornatenton Formation of Germany was described as referable to Torvosaurus.
facts.quote: Also in 2020, a fragmentary maxilla referable to Torvosaurus was described from the middle Callovian Ornatenton Formation of Germany.

facts.statement: The German record suggests megalosaurines may have originated in Europe or that Europe served as a biogeographical hub from the Middle to early Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: This is the record of the genus and suggests that megalosaurines originated in Europe, or at least that Europe was a biogeographical turntable for them from the Middle to the early Late Jurassic.

facts.statement: In 2016, teeth from the Kimmeridgian of Germany were described as likely belonging to Torvosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2016 teeth regarded as likely coming from Torvosaurus were described from the Kimmeridgian of Germany.

facts.statement: Subsequent studies estimate adult Torvosaurus reached 9 to 11 meters in length and weighed up to 2 to 4.4 metric tons.
facts.quote: Subsequent studies have estimated that adults reached 9-11 m in length, and weighed up to 2 - 4.4 MT.

facts.statement: Torvosaurus gurneyi is estimated to have measured 10 to 12 meters in length and weighed 4 to 5 metric tons.
facts.quote: T. gurneyi is estimated to have measured 10-12 m in length and weighed 4 - 5 MT.

facts.statement: Originally, the number of teeth, along with the size and shape of the mouth, differentiated T. gurneyi from T. tanneri.
facts.quote: Among the differentiating features originally recognized between T. gurneyi and T. tanneri are the number of teeth, alongside the size and shape of the mouth.

facts.statement: Later examination suggests the lower tooth count in T. gurneyi may be a preservation artifact, as the exact number cannot be determined.
facts.quote: However, later examination of a new right maxilla, probably belonging to the same individual as the holotype of T. gurneyi, has determined that, while the two species can be distinguished based on the morphology of the maxillary medial wall and interdental plates, the supposedly lower number of maxillary teeth in the Portuguese form may be an artifact of preservation, since it is not possible to know the exact number of teeth in the complete maxilla at the moment.

facts.statement: The German material is distinguished by a temporal difference of about 10 million years and morphological differences, indicating it is a third species outside the T. tanneri and T. gurneyi sister relationship.
facts.quote: The material from Germany is further distinguished by the other two species by a temporal difference of c. 10 Ma and a few morphological differences which indicate that it was the third species outside a sister taxon relationship between T. tanneri and T. gurneyi.

facts.statement: The German maxilla is only 10% smaller than that of T. tanneri, though its ontogenetic stage is unknown.
facts.quote: The material is only 10% smaller than the maxilla of T. tanneri, although the ontogenetic stage of the specimen is unknown.

facts.statement: This indicates derived megalosaurines were among the largest terrestrial predators in the late Middle Jurassic, with only moderate size increases by the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: This indicates that derived megalosaurines were already among the largest terrestrial predators of the late Middle Jurassic, with only a moderate increase in size in the genus by the Late Jurassic.

facts.statement: The premaxilla bore three flat teeth oriented outwardly, with the front edge of each crown overlapping the rear edge of the preceding one.
facts.quote: The frontmost snout bone, the premaxilla, bore three rather flat teeth oriented somewhat outwards with the front edge of the teeth crown overlapping the outer side of the rear edge of the preceding crown.

facts.statement: Like other megalosaurids, the largest teeth in Torvosaurus were located in the second to sixth maxillary alveoli.
facts.quote: Like other megalosaurids, the largest teeth in the mouth of Torvosaurus were in the second to sixth maxillary alveoli.

facts.statement: The antorbital fenestra in Torvosaurus was relatively short.
facts.quote: The antorbital fenestra was relatively short.

facts.statement: The lacrimal bone had a distinctive horn on top and a broad lower end in side view.
facts.quote: The lacrimal bone had a distinctive lacrimal horn on top. Its lower end was broad in side view.

facts.statement: The jugal bone was long and transversely thin.
facts.quote: The jugal was long and transversely thin.

facts.statement: The preserved maxilla of T. gurneyi is 63 cm long, missing 8 cm, indicating a total length of 71 cm.
facts.quote: The maxilla of T. gurneyi is 63 cm in length as preserved but is missing 8 cm of the ventroposterior rim. This indicates the total length of T. gurneyi maxilla is 71 cm in length.

facts.statement: The holotype of T. gurneyi had teeth measuring 10.6 to 11.6 cm in crown height.
facts.quote: The teeth of T. gurneyi were much bigger however, the holotype of T. gurneyi had teeth that measured from 10.6-11.6 cm in crown height.

facts.statement: The largest teeth of T. gurneyi were 15 cm in crown height.
facts.quote: The largest teeth of T. gurneyi were 15 cm in crown height.

facts.statement: Among large theropods in the Lourinhã Formation, only Torvosaurus teeth exceed 7.5 cm in crown height.
facts.quote: Amongst the large theropods of the Lourinhã Formation, only the teeth of Torvosaurus exceed 7.5 cm in crown height.

facts.statement: The balls on the front side of vertebral centra had a wide rim, likened by Britt to a Derby hat.
facts.quote: The balls on the front side of the vertebral centra had a wide rim, a condition by Britt likened to a Derby hat.

facts.statement: The tail base was stiffened vertically by high and wide neural spines.
facts.quote: The tail base was stiffened in the vertical plane by high and in side view wide neural spines.

facts.statement: The entire arm of Torvosaurus was very strong but somewhat short.
facts.quote: The whole of the arm was very strong, but somewhat short.

facts.statement: It is uncertain whether the thumb claw of Torvosaurus was especially enlarged.
facts.quote: Whether the thumb claw was especially enlarged is uncertain.

facts.statement: The pelvis was massively built, with bone skirts between the pubic bones and ischia contacting to form a vaulted closed underside.
facts.quote: The pelvis as a whole was massively built, with the bone skirts between the pubic bones and the ischia contacting each other and forming a vaulted closed underside.

facts.statement: When first described in 1979 by Galton and Jensen, Torvosaurus was classified as a megalosaurid, which remains the current consensus.
facts.quote: When first described in 1979 by Galton and Jensen, Torvosaurus was classified as a megalosaurid, which is the current consensus.

facts.statement: Torvosaurus was later assigned to Carnosauria in 1990, to a basal position in Spinosauroidea in 2003, and to a very basal position in Tetanurae in 1994.
facts.quote: It was later assigned to Carnosauria by Ralph Molnar and colleagues in 1990, then to a basal position in Spinosauroidea by Oliver Walter Mischa Rauhut in 2003, and to a very basal position in Tetanurae by Thomas Holtz in 1994.

facts.statement: None of the alternative classifications (Carnosauria, Spinosauroidea, basal Tetanurae) are supported by present phylogenetic analysis.
facts.quote: All these assignments are not supported by present phylogenetic analysis.

facts.statement: In 1985, Jensen assigned Torvosaurus to its own family, Torvosauridae.
facts.quote: In 1985, Jensen assigned Torvosaurus to a family of its own, Torvosauridae.

facts.statement: Despite support from Paul Sereno and Mateus, Torvosauridae is considered redundant as Torvosaurus is closely related to or the sister species of Megalosaurus within Megalosaurinae.
facts.quote: Despite support for this concept by Paul Sereno and Mateus, it seems redundant because Torvosaurus is closely related to, and perhaps the sister species of, the earlier Megalosaurus within Megalosaurinae.

facts.statement: Though a close relative of Megalosaurus, Torvosaurus appears more advanced or apomorphic.
facts.quote: Though a close relative of Megalosaurus, Torvosaurus is seemingly more advanced, or apomorphic.

facts.statement: Torvosaurus possesses fused interdental plates.
facts.quote: The presence of fused interdental plates

facts.statement: Torvosaurus has pneumatic fossae in the posterior dorsal and anterior caudal vertebrae that are expanded into enlarged, deep openings.
facts.quote: The pneumatic fossae in the posterior dorsal and the anterior caudal vertebrae centra being expanded to form enlarged, deep openings

facts.statement: The type specimen of Torvosaurus tanneri (BYU 2002) was recovered from the Dry Mesa Quarry in the Brushy Basin Member of the Morrison Formation in Montrose County, Colorado.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Torvosaurus tanneri, BYU 2002, was recovered in the Dry Mesa Quarry of the Brushy Basin Member of the Morrison Formation in Montrose County, Colorado.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Torvosaurus tanneri was collected by James A. Jensen and Kenneth Stadtman in 1972.
facts.quote: The specimen was collected by James A. Jensen and Kenneth Stadtman in 1972

facts.statement: The type specimen of Torvosaurus tanneri is housed in the collection of Brigham Young University in Provo, Utah.
facts.quote: This specimen is housed in the collection of Brigham Young University in Provo, Utah.

facts.statement: Studies suggest the Morrison Formation environment included rivers flowing into a basin with a giant saline alkaline lake and extensive wetlands.
facts.quote: Studies suggest that the paleoenvironment of this section of the Morrison Formation included rivers that flowed from the west into a basin that contained a giant, saline alkaline lake and there were extensive wetlands in the vicinity.

facts.statement: The Lourinhã Formation, where Torvosaurus lived, is Kimmeridgian–Tithonian in age.
facts.quote: The Lourinhã Formation is Kimmeridgian–Tithonian in age.

facts.statement: The environment of the Lourinhã Formation was coastal with a strong marine influence.
facts.quote: The environment is coastal and therefore has a strong marine influence.

facts.statement: The highly porous eggshells of Torvosaurus indicate the eggs were buried in the substrate for incubation, similar to modern sea turtles.
facts.quote: However, the eggshells are highly porous, allowing efficient gaseous exchange between the external and internal media, thus indicating the eggs were buried for incubation within substrate in a manner similar to modern seaturtles.

facts.statement: All documented Torvosaurus specimens from the Morrison Formation appear to be similarly sized, likely adult individuals.
facts.quote: All documented Torvosaurus specimens from the Morrison Formation are from similarly sized, likely adult individuals and the lack of immature individuals may be explained by many factors, none of which are mutually exclusive.

facts.statement: Torvosaurus appears to have been the top predator in the Lourinhã Formation ecosystem.
facts.quote: Torvosaurus appears to be the top predator here.

facts.statement: Torvosaurus may have competed with Veterupristisaurus for the position of top predator in the Tendaguru Formation.
facts.quote: Veterupristisaurus (of which it would have possibly competed with to be top predator)

facts.statement: Galton and Jensen interpreted the highly ossified puboischiadic plate of Torvosaurus as evidence that Theropoda was polyphyletic and that Carnosauria evolved independently from carnivorous Prosauropoda.
facts.quote: a very basal trait that Galton & Jensen saw as an indication that Theropoda was polyphyletic, with Carnosauria having independently evolved from carnivorous Prosauropoda

facts.statement: Torvosaurus lived between the late Middle Jurassic and late Upper Jurassic, approximately 165 to 148 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió entre finales período Jurásico Medio y finales del Jurásico Superior, entre 165 a 148 millones de años

facts.statement: Torvosaurus fossils have been found in what is now Europe, North America, Africa, and South America.
facts.quote: en lo que hoy es Europa, Norteamérica, África y Sudamérica

facts.statement: Possible Torvosaurus remains in South America are found only in the Tacuarembó Formation of Uruguay.
facts.quote: Within South America, possible Torvosaurus remains are only present within the Tacuarembó Formation of Uruguay.

facts.statement: The Tacuarembó Formation environment was dominated by rivers, streams, and lakes, indicated by fluvial to lacustrine sedimentary rocks.
facts.quote: Because the formation was laid down in fluvial to lacustrine sandstones, siltstones, and mudstones, this indicates that the environment of the formation would have been dominated by rivers, streams, and lakes.

facts.statement: If present, Torvosaurus was likely the apex predator in the Tacuarembó Formation, though it may have competed with Ceratosaurus.
facts.quote: If present, Torvosaurus would probably have been the apex predator in the Tacuarembó Formation, although it may have been rivalled by cf. Ceratosaurus.

facts.statement: Torvosaurus and Ceratosaurus likely preferred waterways and had lower, sinuous bodies suited for forest and underbrush terrain.
facts.quote: Torvosaurus and Ceratosaurus may have preferred to be active around waterways and had lower, more sinuous, bodies that would have given them an advantage in forest and underbrush terrains

facts.statement: Torvosaurus may have been specialized in opening and dismembering exceptionally large sauropod carcasses due to its large skull, teeth, and powerful body.
facts.quote: Torvosaurus, with its large skull and teeth and large, powerful, and lithe body may have been specialized in opening up and dismembering exceptionally large sauropod carcasses.

facts.statement: Bite marks on Allosaurus larger than any known specimen suggest either increased site diversity or evidence of Allosaurus cannibalism.
facts.quote: The result either increases the known diversity of the site based on ichnological evidence alone or represents powerful evidence of cannibalism in Allosaurus.

facts.statement: The type species Torvosaurus tanneri was named in 1979.
facts.quote: En 1979 se nombró a la especie tipo Torvosaurus tanneri.

facts.statement: Torvosaurus tanneri was a large, robust, bipedal carnivore that could grow to nearly 10 meters in length.
facts.quote: T. tanneri era un carnívoro bípedo grande, de constitución robusta que podía crecer a una longitud cercana a los 10 metros.

facts.statement: Based on bone morphology, Torvosaurus is believed to have had short but very powerful arms.
facts.quote: Basándose en la morfología ósea de Torvosaurus, se cree que tenía brazos cortos pero muy poderosos.

facts.statement: Torvosaurus is classified in the family Megalosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Megalosauridae

facts.statement: Torvosaurus is classified in the subfamily Megalosaurinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Megalosaurinae

facts.statement: The type species of Torvosaurus is Torvosaurus tanneri.
facts.quote: type_species: Torvosaurus tanneri

facts.statement: Torvosaurus gurneyi was described by Hendrickx and Mateus in 2014.
facts.quote: subdivision: Torvosaurus gurneyi Hendrickx & Mateus, 2014

facts.statement: It is debated whether Epanterias is a distinct species or simply a large individual of Allosaurus.
facts.quote: T. tanneri estuvo entre los mayores carnívoros de su tiempo, junto a Epanterias, el cual puede ser en realidad un individuo grande de Allosaurus

facts.statement: It is debated whether bite marks on Allosaurus represent a separate large taxon like Torvosaurus or evidence of Allosaurus cannibalism.
facts.quote: The result either increases the known diversity of the site based on ichnological evidence alone or represents powerful evidence of cannibalism in Allosaurus.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the bite marks could belong to an unusually large Allosaurus or a separate taxon like Torvosaurus not yet found at the quarry.
facts.quote: The extrapolations are instead coherent, either with an unusually large specimen of Allosaurus or a separate large taxon like Torvosaurus which is not known from the quarry.

facts.statement: Torvosaurus was an enormous predator with an estimated maximum body length of 10 meters and a mass of 4 to 5 tonnes for both T. tanneri and T. gurneyi.
facts.quote: Torvosaurus fue un enorme depredador, con una longitud corporal máxima estimada en 10 metros y una masa de 4 a 5 toneladas tanto para T. tanneri como T. gurneyi

facts.statement: In 2014, the Portuguese species T. gurneyi was estimated to be 10 meters long and weigh between 3.6 and 4.5 metric tonnes.
facts.quote: En 2014 se estimó 10 metros y una masa de 3,6 a 4,5 toneladas métricas para la especie portuguesa T. gurneyi

facts.statement: Claims based on incomplete remains of Edmarka rex and "Brontoraptor" suggest the American species T. tanneri could reach up to 12 meters in length and over 4 tonnes in mass.
facts.quote: Se han realizado afirmaciones que indican tamaños aún mayores para la especie americana T. tanneri de hasta 12 metros de largo y más de 4 toneladas con base en restos incompletos de Edmarka rex y "Brontoraptor"

facts.statement: The synonym Edmarka rex was named because it was assumed to rival Tyrannosaurus rex in length.
facts.quote: El sinónimo Edmarka rex fue nombrado porque se supuso que rivalizaría con Tyrannosaurus rex en longitud

facts.statement: Torvosaurus had an elongated and narrow snout with a profile fold just above the nostrils.
facts.quote: Torvosaurus tenía un hocico alargado y estrecho, con un pliegue de perfil justo sobre las fosas nasales

facts.statement: The premaxilla, the bone at the front of the snout, had three flattened teeth oriented slightly outward.
facts.quote: El hueso más al frente en el hocico, el premaxilar, tiene tres dientes aplanados orientados ligeramente hacia afuera

facts.statement: The maxilla was high and had at least eleven elongated teeth.
facts.quote: El maxilar era alto y tenía al menos once dientes alargados

facts.statement: The eye orbit was high with a pointed lower end.
facts.quote: La órbita ocular era alta con un extremo inferior en punta

facts.statement: The lower front side of the quadrate bone was hollowed out by a depression shaped like a tear.
facts.quote: La parte inferior del lado frontal del hueso cuadrado estaba ahuecado por una depresión en forma de lágrima

facts.statement: The base of the tail was rigid in the vertical plane due to neural spines that were high and very wide in lateral view.
facts.quote: La base de la cola era rígida en el plano vertical por espinas neurales que eran altas y muy anchas en vista lateral

facts.statement: The upper arm was very robust, while the forearm was short and strong.
facts.quote: La parte superior del brazo era muy robusta; el antebrazo era corto y fuerte

facts.statement: In the pelvis, the ilium resembled that of Megalosaurus, having a high form that was short at the front and had a longer, tapered posterior tip.
facts.quote: En la pelvis, el ilion se parecía al de Megalosaurus y tenía una forma alta, corta en la parte frontal y una punta posterior más larga de forma ahusada

facts.statement: The complete pelvis had a massive constitution, with bone flaps between the pubis and ischia contacting each other to form a closed vault-like lower part.
facts.quote: La pelvis completa tenía una constitución masiva, con faldones de hueso entre los pubis y los isquiones contactándose entre sí y formando una parte inferior en forma de bóveda cerrada

facts.statement: The upper jaw of T. tanneri has more than 11 teeth, while that of T. gurneyi has fewer.
facts.quote: Mientras que la mandíbula superior de T. tanneri tiene más de 11 dientes, y la de T. gurneyi menos

facts.statement: It is debated whether the lower number of maxillary teeth in T. gurneyi is a valid distinction, as a later examination suggests it may be a conservation artifact despite differences in medial maxillary wall morphology and interdental plates.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, un examen posterior de un nuevo maxilar derecho probablemente perteneciente al mismo individuo que el holotipo de T. gurneyi ha determinado que si bien las dos especies se pueden distinguir en función de la morfología de la pared medial maxilar y las placas interdentales, el número supuestamente menor de dientes maxilares en la forma portuguesa puede ser un artefacto de conservación

facts.statement: Torvosaurus is characterized by a shallow fossa in the maxilla that lacks a maxillary fenestra crossing the bony wall.
facts.quote: La presencia de una fosa poco profunda en el maxilar, carece de la fenestra maxillaris atravesando la pared ósea

facts.statement: Pneumatic fossae in the centers of posterior dorsal and anterior caudal vertebrae are expanded, forming large and deep openings.
facts.quote: Las fosas neumáticas en los centros de las vértebras dorsales posteriores y las caudales anteriores están expandidos, formando aberturas grandes y profundas

facts.statement: The puboischiatic plate is highly ossified, with paired bony plates on both sides connecting and closing the lower part of the pelvis.
facts.quote: La placa puboisquiática está muy osificada (las placas óseas pares, en ambos lados, se conectan y cierran en la parte inferior de la pelvis

facts.statement: According to Rauhut in 2000, there is a distal expansion of the ischial axis with a prominent lateral crest in the middle and an oval silhouette when viewed laterally.
facts.quote: De acuerdo con Rauhut en 2000 hay una expansión distal del eje del isquion con una prominente cresta lateral en el medio y una silueta oval cuando se mira en vista lateral

facts.statement: Cervical vertebrae are opisthocoelous with a pronounced flattened border around the anterior ball-shaped joint.
facts.quote: Las vértebras cervicales son opistocelosas con un pronunciado borde aplanado alrededor de la articulación en forma de bola anterior

facts.statement: A transverse fenestra is located in the neural arch of dorsal vertebrae in front of the hypophysis.
facts.quote: Una fenestra transversa se sitúa en el arco neural de las vértebras dorsales en frents del hiposfeno

facts.statement: The parent group of Torvosaurus is Megalosaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Megalosaurinae

facts.statement: Torvosaurus belongs to the family Megalosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Megalosauridae

facts.statement: Torvosaurus is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Torvosaurus is Torvosaurus tanneri.
facts.quote: Type species: Torvosaurus tanneri
